source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Classify it as sharps waste because any item containing visible blood belongs in a puncture-resistant sharps container.","B":"Classify it as pharmaceutical waste because blood-contaminated material is disposed through the medication-waste stream.","C":"Classify the dressing as regulated waste because it would release blood in a liquid or semiliquid state if compressed.","D":"Classify it as ordinary solid waste because dressings are excluded from regulated waste regardless of saturation."}}
source_row.rationale: OSHA defines regulated waste to include contaminated items that would release blood or other potentially infectious material in a liquid or semiliquid state if compressed. The stem was narrowed from the vague phrase 'blood-soaked' to the regulatory criterion that determines classification.
source_row.source_detail: Definition of regulated waste under 29 CFR 1910.1030(b) Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A dressing is saturated with blood and would release blood if compressed. How should this item be classified for disposal?
